steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Arrange sliced apples evenly in the bottom of the prepared baking dish. Pour water over apples.
Combine cake mix, brown sugar, and cinnamon in a medium bowl. Stir in melted butter until thoroughly blended and crumbly. Sprinkle over apples.
Bake in the preheated oven until bubbly and topping is browned, 50 to 55 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Apple Crisp
raw_recipe.description: This apple crisp with a cake mix-brown sugar streusel topping is baked in a 9x13-inch dish until bubbly for a warm dessert, great for feeding a crowd.

video.description: In this video, we turn the season’s bounty of apples into a warm and comforting dessert. Apple slices are topped with a crumble made from a package of white cake mix, brown sugar and cinnamon. We’ll bake this in the oven and serve warm with vanilla ice cream.
video.name: Easy Apple Crisp

review.reviewBody: This recipe was so simple, yet so delicious! Some changes I recommend that other users may have also recommended: use 3/4 water instead, use only 3/4c brown sugar (it was a bit too sweet for my taste), use large green apples, bake for only 40-45 minutes, and add rolled oats to the cake mixture (i added about 1/2c). The rolled oats give the topping a crispier, yet mildly chewy consistency. Also, eating this a la mode with vanilla ice cream = HEAVEN!

FALULOUS!!! Took others suggestions and used 3/4 cup apple cider in place of water; omited sugar, and added 1 cup oatmeal to cake mix topping. The whole pan is gone and my family is clammering for more. Brother-in-law got jiffy cake mix by mistake, and I used 2 boxes to great success. Will make again and again, and everyone asked for the recipe.

I used JOSIEMAI's revisions: use 3/4 cup water, use only 3/4c brown sugar, bake for only 40-45 minutes, and add rolled oats to the cake mixture. Then for my own revision, I used spice cake mix instead of white cake mix, which made it so flavorful and perfect.
The family loved this!!! 
I made it Friday night and again Saturday night since it was so requested and the whole dish had been eaten the night before. 
Definitely a recipe that I will keep and make many times.

I started with this recipe and made three changes.
- I combined apple, pear, and raisins and added 1/4 cup of brown sugar directly onto the fruit.
- I added a cup of oatmeal to give more texture and crunch.
- doubled the butter - doubled the cinnamon for more flavor
The recipe was delicious and my house smelled like winter holidays. Was perfect served warm with ice cream.
This recipe rocks, and adapts to changes easily (see other comments!) I used spice cake mix, more apples to fill 2 8×8 pans. Baked longer to get a brown crunch. Perfect!

This was very similar to my mom's apple crisp that she made when I was a kid. I followed her recipe by using two cans of apple pie filling (Target brand worked great), no water needed, yellow cake mix, and after spreading the cake mixture over the apples, I melted 1/4 cup of butter and sprinkled over the top layer with a little nutmeg. Didn't go the full time on this recipe...but about 45 minutes instead. This was so good that I had to be disciplined at only back for seconds...once! Enjoy!

2 cans filling is not enough. This tasted great for Thanksgiving dessert, and everyone loved it. Here are my notes, changes and 1 problem. I decided to use the pie filling, as poster gave that option. The 2 can option was no way to be enough. Used 3 cans (21 oz) Duncan Hines More Fruit Apple Pie Filling. Left out the water as directed when using the canned filling. Used Duncan Hines Butter Golden Cake mix. Cut the brown sugar to 1/4 cup, due the the sweetness of of the filling and cake mix. Was perfect. Sprinkled lightly the filling with cinnamon. Added 1 tsp cinnamon into the cake mixture. added 3/4 cup rolled oats. Following the suggestions by others, I increased the butter to 6.5 tb, instead of 4. Now comes the problem. The topping of butter, cake mix, rolled oats and cinnamon did not get very crumbly.,only about 20%. The remainder of the mixture was like a thick brownie mix. I added in 1/4 cup more rolled oats. Helped a little, but not a lot. It had to be hand spread over the apple mixture, a little difficult. Next time I will try with the recipe of only 4 tb. Cooked for only 45 mins. However, while visually not a crumbly looking topping, the flavor was still great! Excellent recipe and will make again. Served warm with vanilla ice cream.

Great recipe but I did make a few changes as I always do. I used about 10 cups of apples( Granny Smith and a few cortlands) To the apples I added 1 1/2 tsp vanilla, 1 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp nutmeg. and a pinch of all spice ( you could use apple pie spice 2 tsp) I placed those in the pan and added 3/4 cup of water. To the white cake mix I added only 3/4 cup of brown sugar, 1/4 tsp cinnamon3/4 cups of rolled oats add the melted butter and crumble over the top of apples. Made this twice with rave reviews I baked mine about 55 minutes, I like a little crisper apple not mushy.

This was amazing and so easy to make. I used the 2 cans of apple pie filling by Duncan Hines. It says to not add water if using the filling but I did anyway. I dumped the cans into a greased baking dish and topped with some water and than added the cake mixture. Tip: I checked it when it had about 20 min to go and I still seen some of the powder cake mix on top so I added more water to the spots that needed it. I honestly didn't think it would taste so good. Topped it with vanilla ice cream!!

This apple crisp was so easy and yummy! I used salted butter which gave the topping a delicious sweet and salty flavor. Per suggestions in the reviews, I used only 1/4 cup of brown sugar and no white sugar and 1/2 cup of apple juice instead of water for the apples. It was plenty sweet and I might use no sugar at all next time (and there will definitely be a next time). I also eyeballed about 1/2 cup of quick cooking oats into to the topping. I added nutmeg and a dash of ground cloves to the apples as well. Thank you very much for the recipe!
Used two more apples, cut water to 3/4 cup, added finely chopped pecans on top at end. It was delicious!
I didn’t use apples at all. I used peaches and pears! It came out beautifully and tasted terrific!

Delicious....I made same changes as the Others did after reading the reviews.. Next time making it I will cut back to 1/4 c. br sugar & but I did add a few crunched up walnuts.next time I want to swap out for peaches ...it's a keeper!!!! sugar
Amazing apple crisp recipe. Turned out very moist and it was absolutely soo yummy and very easy to make. I'm gonna have to make it again!
It turned out awesome. Everyone in the family loved it
The topping is so crispy. Loved it!
I learned how to peel apples. Thank you for this recipe.
